blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Self-supervised joint embedding learning aligns representations of augmented views while regularizing their distribution to prevent collapse. Regularization aims to shape the overall representation distribution, but most joint embedding methods restrict its computation to the active minibatch. We propose out-of-batch regularization, which maintains a dataset-level state in CPU memory and uses globally constructed per-instance targets during minibatch training. Evaluated on natural images and biomedical datasets, these anchors approximate the full-dataset regularization gradient more faithfully than conventional minibatch estimation at small batch sizes. Applications to contrastive (SimCLR) and non-contrastive (SIGReg) approaches show consistent improvement over the corresponding in-batch objectives for image classification, minority-class performance under controlled imbalance, instance retrieval, and continued self-supervised pretraining, with the largest gains at small batch sizes. These results suggest that dataset-level regularization can be decoupled from minibatch optimization, making batch size an optimization choice that does not affect the geometry of the regularizer.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Joint-embedding architectures (JEAs) ( Chen et al., 2020a ; Grill et al., 2020 ; Caron et al., 2021 ; Bardes et al., 2021 ) have been the dominant paradigm for visual self-supervised representation learning. Applications range from 3D medical image analysis ( Tang et al., 2022 ) to 3D scene reconstruction ( Wang et al., 2025 ) and vision–language alignment ( Radford et al., 2021 ) . They use augmentations to create a pretraining objective based on view invariance. Anti-collapse regularization complements this objective to prevent trivial solutions ( Chen and He, 2021 ) . While different regularization mechanisms have been proposed over the years, most of them act on the embeddings of the current minibatch (or a few recent batches with EMA) that might be too small to represent the dataset under memory or optimization constraints.
blocks.zh: 联合嵌入式建筑(JEAs)(Chen等,2020年a; Grill等, 2020; Caron等, 2021; Bardes等, 2021.) 一直是视觉自导自演学习的主导范式. 应用范围从3D医学影像分析(Tang等,2022年)到3D场景重建(Wang等,2025年)和视觉-语言对接(Radford等,2021年). 他们利用增强功能,根据观点的偏差,建立预训目标. 反冲突规范化是对这一目标的补充,以防止微不足道的解决办法(Chen and He, 2021). 虽然多年来提出了不同的规范化机制,但大多数机制都对当前小批量(或最近几批与EMA)的嵌入作用,这些小批量可能太小,无法在内存或优化限制下代表数据集.

blocks.en:
The bottleneck is particularly relevant for high-dimensional inputs, including high-resolution images and 3D volumes, where each sample requires more activation memory. Such applications are thus often limited to small-batch training. The problem worsens for imbalanced data, where rare classes may contribute only a few examples to each batch ( Jing et al., 2021 ) . The simple solution of using a larger batch is constrained by hardware ( Gao et al., 2021 ) , and even when a large batch is possible, it may not be ideal for optimization. On small datasets, using a large fraction of the training samples per batch leaves few parameter updates per epoch. Masters and Luschi (2018) also report that larger batches can
require more careful choice of the learning rate and training duration. The batch size needed to estimate a population regularizer can therefore differ from the best batch size for optimization.

blocks.en: We propose a framework that moves the statistical context of SSL regularizers from the active batch to the dataset-level state. We maintain a detached, dataset-indexed state in CPU memory. A periodic refresh encodes the training set and constructs globally optimized targets, while online steps retrieve only the current samples’ targets (Fig. 1 ). Thus, the support of the anti-collapse component is no longer limited by the batch size or GPU capacity.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Collapse prevention in joint embedding training. Joint-embedding methods must preserve informative variation while aligning
views. Contrastive objectives achieve this through negative-sample repulsion ( Oord et al., 2018 ; Chen et al., 2020a ) , linking alignment to
hyperspherical uniformity for normalized representations ( Wang and Isola, 2020 ) . To avoid explicit negatives, Barlow Twins and
VICReg constrain correlations and moments ( Zbontar et al., 2021 ; Bardes et al., 2021 ) , while SIGReg matches projected
distributions to a Gaussian ( Balestriero and LeCun, 2025 ) . Other approaches
prevent collapse through balanced assignments in SwAV ( Caron et al., 2020 ) or asymmetry, teachers, and stop-gradient
in BYOL, DINO, and SimSiam ( Grill et al., 2020 ; Caron et al., 2021 ; Chen and He, 2021 ) .
These approaches establish how to prevent collapse, but they have to assume that the active batch is representative of the dataset.

blocks.en:
Assigned targets and dataset-indexed representations. Constructing targets separately from encoder updates also provides broader context. Noise-vector assignment ( Bojanowski and Joulin, 2017 ) , dataset-feature clustering ( Caron et al., 2018 ) , and balanced self-labeling through optimal transport ( Asano et al., 2019 ) organize representation learning around assigned targets.
Our anchors instead retain per-instance correspondence and are reconstructed
from current representations under a specified continuous geometry. DIET
also uses sample identity, predicting datum indices as classes ( Balestriero, 2023 ) . IConE, the conceptually closest recent approach ( Almpanakis and Kreshuk, 2026 ) , separates collapse prevention from encoder alignment through a jointly optimized N × d N\times d table of auxiliary instance embeddings. Its regularization maintains a persistent global parameter space during training and evaluates an N × N N\times N similarity matrix each step. OOB instead periodically constructs detached per-instance targets from a chosen population-level regularizer, stores these targets in CPU memory, and retrieves only those required by the active minibatch. This decouples online training from the global computation while supporting different regularizers.

blocks.en: 4.2 Oracle gradient analysis

blocks.en:
Using the fixed objective from section 3.5 , we compare
minibatch sampling error with cache staleness at training
checkpoints. Figure 2 A–B shows that limited batch context can change the
direction of regularization and can produce gradients that oppose the full-dataset objective. As batch size gets bigger, its regularization gradient agrees more with the oracle. A fresh cache recovers the oracle exactly, but its agreement deteriorates as
the encoder changes ( Figure 2 C–D). This deterioration is slower at later checkpoints, where cached
gradients remain informative across more online updates. The results confirm that minibatch and
cached estimators face different limitations: incomplete population context
versus temporal staleness. When training with small batches, periodic dataset-level regularization is clearly beneficial, while the update schedule should depend on the training stage.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 5 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en: We introduced out-of-batch (OOB) regularization, which decouples population-level representation regularization from minibatch optimization through periodically constructed dataset-level targets. Across contrastive and non-contrastive objectives, OOB more faithfully recovers the full-dataset regularization signal and improves representation quality, particularly in cases where small minibatches poorly approximate the full population. Our results show that the active minibatch does not need to define the population over which representation geometry is regularized.
blocks.zh: 我们推行了 " 包外 " (OOB)正规化,通过定期制定数据集一级目标,将人口级别的代表正规化与 " 小包 " 优化脱钩。 在整个不同和非相互矛盾的目标中,OOB更忠实地恢复了完整的数据集规范化信号并改进了代表质量,特别是在小型小炮管不完全接近全体人口的情况下。 我们的结果表明,活跃的小批量不需要界定几何特征正规化的人口。

blocks.en: OOB replaces minibatch sampling error with a different trade-off: dataset-level state must be stored and periodically refreshed as the encoder evolves. Understanding this trade-off at larger scales remains an important direction. More broadly, our results motivate separating globally coupled representation objectives from the minibatch updates used to train the encoder, with regularizer-specific constructions providing a possible route to population-aware learning beyond the objectives studied here.

blocks.en:
The oracle study differentiates the projected-Gaussian anti-collapse loss with
respect to each probe representation. Consequently, every “gradient” is a
vector in representation space, not the scalar loss and not the full network
parameter gradient. The full-dataset reference recomputes ranks and Gaussian
quantile assignments from the current representations of every training
sample. The minibatch estimator computes the same construction from a sampled
batch, whereas the cached estimator reuses full-dataset assignments made at an
earlier encoder state. At every cache age, the reference itself is recomputed
at the current encoder state; cached agreement is therefore measured against
the current population objective rather than against the reference at refresh.

visible for the underrepresented classes and, in many settings, for the worst

frequency weighting. The label-aware oracle diagnostic in the main paper
therefore separates two claims: OOB state can estimate a chosen population
objective more faithfully, but changing that objective to be class-balanced
requires an explicit weighting decision.
